item.text: The existing helper is currently async-free in practice but not robust: it parses every prefixed key before validating its suffix, and returns `0` on empty/invalid storage. I’ll change it to return `number | null`, validate suffixes before reading session content, preserve last-active preference, and update the public-session call plus test expectations. I’ll also check whether the drive-store copy needs matching behavior.

`resumeSession` requires a numeric ID, so the hook should skip the resume attempt when there is no valid persisted local ID; this also avoids passing `null` into its API. The shared drive-store copy contains only the UID lookup, so the changed utility is only in the Drive app. I’m now implementing a synchronous, read-only scan that ignores unrelated and malformed-suffix keys, with invalid JSON handled as no usable ID.

The first edit introduced unnecessary block scopes while narrowing the loops; I’m cleaning that up and making malformed session JSON non-fatal per entry, so one corrupt value won’t hide another valid persisted session. Parsing errors in active-ping metadata still follow the existing error-report path.

The behavior and regression cases are in place. I’m refining error handling so malformed data for one key cannot discard other valid sessions, then I’ll run the existing Drive utility test and type-check the app surface.

The targeted Jest run is underway. The diff is clean and confirms unrelated keys and nonnumeric suffixes are excluded; the lookup only inspects localStorage and never mutates it. Next I’ll collect the test result and run TypeScript checking if the focused test passes.
The test process hasn’t emitted output yet, likely due to workspace startup; I’m waiting briefly for its completion rather than starting overlapping checks.
The test command is still silent after roughly 20 seconds. I’ll give it another short interval; if it remains stuck, I’ll inspect the process state and report that accurately.

Implemented the persisted-session lookup fix. `getLastPersistedLocalID` now returns `number | null`, considers only numeric `ps-` keys, and leaves storage untouched. The public bookmark hook skips `resumeSession` when no valid ID exists, and regression tests cover empty storage, malformed suffixes, invalid JSON, and unrelated keys.
